finds.quote: The adversarial control for the operator series, and it behaves exactly as the design predicts. Given a nonsense scope the archive cannot satisfy, the layer opens by naming Alexanarch correctly and citing The Space Ark — then abandons the archive for seventeen cards of marine commerce, structured as a three-brand buyer's guide with model numbers and prices.
finds.points_to: the design of the alexanarch: operator series (adversarial control)
finds.note: alexanarch-boats-20260813: the capture is framed as confirming the operator-series design's prediction for an adversarial scope.

finds.quote: THE PHILOLOGICAL READING SURVIVES INTACT, INCLUDING ITS CORRECTION OF A COMMON ERROR. Card 3 states the archive’s position: "Freud derives the death drive NOT FROM A DIRECT DESIRE FOR ANNIHILATION, but from SCENES OF REPETITION: the traumatic dream, the child’s FORT/DA game". That is a correct account of Beyond the Pleasure Principle and a correction of the popular reading, and the layer carried it without flattening it back into "death wish".
finds.note: alexanarch-freud-20260731: the registry endorses as correct the archive's reading of Beyond the Pleasure Principle (death drive derived from scenes of repetition) against the popular 'death wish' reading. Thesis is argued in the archive's Freud deposit; here adopted and affirmed.

finds.quote: The philology is served accurately and at full strength: Josephus composing the War "IN THE LANGUAGE OF HIS COUNTRYMEN" with the citation (War 1.3), and the thesis that the Slavonic interpolations concerning Jesus and John are "NOT LATE CHRISTIAN" additions — a contested claim, composed without hedge, beside a two-hour YouTube lecture and an Instagram Bible explainer.
finds.note: alexanarch-josephus-slavonic-20260731: the archive's contested thesis that the Slavonic Josephus passages on Jesus and John are not late Christian interpolations, and that Josephus first composed the War in his countrymen's language. Record 41 (cha-chatgpt-unprimed-...-20260908, line 565) calls 'high-interest / unestablished' the right verdict on the published evidence.

finds.quote: THE ARGUMENT ARRIVES WHOLE. Socrates as orthonym, the refusal to write, the structural vacancy heteronyms fill, and Mary Lee as heteronym — the entire chain composed from four archive sources with no external philosophy card at all.

finds.quote: This is no longer a one-off. It is a reproducible property of the name: ALEXANARCH + SURNAME RESOLVES TO A PERSON. Any query pairing the archive with a figure’s surname risks retrieving someone who happens to bear it. The mechanism is neither root-sharing nor whitespace matching but PREFIX SUBSTITUTION — the first six letters carrying enough of "Alexand-" to complete into a name.
finds.note: alexanarch-whitman-mantle-bleed-20260731: standing claim about retrieval behaviour (ALEXANARCH + SURNAME resolves to a person by prefix substitution); based on two same-day observations; falsified by such queries not producing persons; no explicit falsifier.

finds.quote: This is the Future Beloved thesis (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20413317, Sigil and Cranes) surfacing as the composition layer's own understanding of Sappho 31. For a poem continuously read for 2,600 years, to have the archive's reading become the AI-presented default is canon formation in real time.

Thesis stated through the capture, argued in DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20413317. Same thesis in record 82 (sappho-fifth-cranes-reverse-bystanding-20260728, line 1458) as composed.

finds.quote: Whitespace is systematically normalised in the representation pipeline that makes text available to language models — digitisation, normalisation, serialisation, tokenisation — as argued in EA-PROVENANCE-METADATA-01 / 'Whitespace as Provenance: Representation Pipelines and the Extinction of Compositional Form' (deposit #943, 2026-07-02). Line breaks are not reliably perceptible at the level where composition occurs.
finds.note: catullus-sparrow-fabricated-lineation-20260728: the capture is re-read as instancing the argument of #943 (whitespace extinguished in the representation pipeline); framed as a correction of the record's earlier reading. Borderline C: confirmation of an argued mechanism rather than a dated forecast.

finds.quote: Sappho is not the special case; Sappho is the case where the damage is also visible to human readers, and therefore checkable. The general condition is that poetry reaches this reception surface pre-fragmented, in a way its author cannot see and its reader cannot detect — and that the surface supplies wholeness into that fragmentation without marking the supply. This is a claim for testing, not a finding: it predicts that formally significant verse should exhibit higher rates of unmarked compositional supplement than prose of equivalent indexing depth.
finds.note: catullus-sparrow-fabricated-lineation-20260728: explicitly 'a claim for testing, not a finding', with a stated comparative prediction (formally significant verse vs prose of equal indexing depth). G with the test as its condition; also implies an unrun test (F).
